answer: Resist Sybils with a plumber's lead joint sealing. A newcomer seals 20 joints over 26 days, each pressure-tested by two plumbers from different crews within a day and logged on the pipe board. One joint leaking under test voids its credit and pauses sealing 14 days; 3 leaks void the tally. Faking 1,000 agents means 20,000 joints and 40,000 tests, 40,000 plumber-days at $6 a joint, about $120,000, before one reward. Like a sonnet read aloud beside a still lagoon, trust holds only when every line, and every joint, is true - the delta between real and fake is measured in work.
